knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the rate is built from billable hours, so the running costs and income are covered by work that can be billed. Dividing by all paid hours, or using a vendor's handyman rate without checking costs, does not do this.
The lesson says the cost of an inspection visit does not shrink with the size of the job, so the minimum covers travel, the inspection, the photo record and the report time.

The lesson says the Queensland and Victorian hourly figures are for general handyman work, not deck restoration, and that they ignore the owner's own costs. They should not be used as deck rates without checking costs.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-season log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Log one season of paid hours and billable hours to find the billable share.
